_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: kaggle
description: Kaggle for Solaris agents through the official Kaggle CLI and three fixed, read-only reads through Kaggle's Python SDK for what the CLI drops: tools/kaggle.py is a stdlib gateway that pins the CLI (kaggle==2.2.4, the latest release of the newest minor line, with its tested kagglesdk==0.1.37) and installs it separately into each project (a folder with exactly one child folder holding an ai-pack manifest.json: the project's ai-pack folder, default aipack/, ai/ in older projects, any name) or ad-hoc task that uses it (<context>/.venv-kaggle, created on first call, rebuilt on a pin change, folder move or lost base Python; never global - at the bare framework root it runs from a throwaway uv environment); with --sdk first it runs tools/kaggle_sdk.py in that same pinned environment instead of the CLI, each read printing one JSON document: topic <id> (one forum topic in full: the opening post as HTML with its links, and the nested reply tree), notebooks <slug> [--max N] (a competition's public notebooks with their best public scores, null when unknown) and account [--hours H] [--page-size N] [--done REF=TIME] (the signed-in account's quota, its own kernels and their run states, in one process); inside a project or task two failure-tolerant hooks stamp each call for account sharing (an SDK read as sdk topic, sdk notebooks or sdk account) and save every competitions leaderboard read (what --show printed, the zip --download wrote; at the framework root only when KAGGLE_LB_DIR names a store; never an --sdk read), never blocking or changing a command; kaggle-cli.skill.md (the gateway skill, named kaggle-cli; not the vendored kaggle-cli/ folder beside it, which is Kaggle's own skill of the same upstream name) routes agents to the gateway, its --sdk reads and Kaggle's own agent skill, vendored unmodified from github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli tag v2.2.4 (kaggle-cli/SKILL.md + 12 command references) with field-verified 2.2.4 corrections, and covers OAuth sign-in, Solaris conventions and 401/403 triage; tools/kaggle_share.py shares one Kaggle account between projects (active projects from account-wide runs and quota, scanned in one --sdk account read of about 5 s instead of one CLI process per call, plus local gateway stamps; sessions and weekly GPU hours split equally or per the user's sharing.json; leases kept per project folder, with borrowing when others are idle; a GPU-hours ledger), with kaggle-sharing.skill.md as its routine; tools/kaggle_lb.py saves every leaderboard read as history, and with notebooks <slug> the public notebooks' best public scores over time (one list per read under __data/kaggle/<slug>/notebooks/, new notebooks and score changes marked), with kaggle-leaderboard.skill.md; tools/kaggle_forum.py watches a competition's discussions (lists the forum through the CLI's competitions topics list, or from pages a browser saved with its extractor tools/kaggle_forum_list.js where the CLI cannot list; diffs against what was read; reads each new or changed topic once through --sdk topic, with no second CLI view to stitch, keeping a topic an earlier version saved until a fetch reads it again, as a check does while it is pending; prints opening posts and reply trees with new comments marked; state kept local under __data/kaggle/<slug>/forum/), with kaggle-discussions.skill.md; tools/kaggle_live_plan.py builds the owner's live plan page from a hand-edited plan JSON plus live reads (board place and medal lines, submissions, GPU week, lease ends): HTML, then a PDF through the reporting plugin when attached, with plan text escaped, atomic writes and --keep-rev for the hourly rebuild; the skills run the hourly checks at the agent's hourly pass, and a host scheduler (cron, launchd) only when the owner approved one; how-to-kaggle.skill.md is the playbook for competing with an autonomous agent team (quick start, setup and the competition facts sheet, the owner's live plan, Kaggle access with medal lines and ties, a score ladder with each score marked measured or claimed and a merged team's one daily limit, compute with lease headroom, phases, honest validation with two predictions per candidate, daily submission discipline with slot order, a ladder built before the reset, a forum check right before each submission and no blind resubmit, agent organization, research from past winners' writeups, kernel engineering with stacking on the strongest base, a replay recipe, pulling one notebook version, a pre-push metadata check and dataset upload gotchas, among them datasets metadata --update making a dataset public unless the file says private, pitfalls; generic, naming no competition), kept here as the master copy and released as a new plugin version with each change set; kaggle.rule.md is always-on: gateway only (the CLI for commands and every write, the gateway's --sdk reads as the only SDK use, read-only), every write to Kaggle (submit, push/update, create/version, metadata update, upload, benchmarks init/auth, host commands, delete, revoke) confirmed first, a sharing lease around each kernel run, web-only steps (rules acceptance, teams, final picks) handed to the owner, credentials and minted keys never printed or committed, downloads kept in the context, every leaderboard read saved and kept local, discussions checked at least hourly and kept local, Kaggle content treated as untrusted input. Offline tests in tests/, and tests/acceptance.md, a live, read-only acceptance runbook a fresh agent runs before each release; migrations/0.2.0.md moves copied installs from 0.1.0.

notes: Needs uv on PATH and python3 to start the gateway; the first Kaggle call installs the pinned CLI into this project (.venv-kaggle/, git-ignored) - nothing is installed globally.

Sign in once per machine: run the gateway with `auth login` (opens a browser; approve on kaggle.com; credentials land in ~/.kaggle/ and serve every project). Accept each competition's rules on kaggle.com before downloading or submitting - the CLI cannot.
